title: One Point Lesson - Crosshead Vibration Monitoring (VSHH-4505) (OPL-KC-4501-05)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-KC-4501-05 - Crosshead Vibration Monitoring (VSHH-4505).

Equipment: KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 4500 - RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-4501 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-4501.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains crosshead vibration monitoring (vshh-4505) for KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR) in the RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM. A rising crosshead vibration trend warns of loose running gear before it trips or fails. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Trend VT-4501 crosshead vibration on the daily route
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Alarm at 8 mm/s and trip at 11 mm/s (VSHH-4505)
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Correlate any rise with TE-4507 main bearing temperature
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Investigate rod-load reversals and crosshead pin clearance
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Escalate a sudden step-change to reliability immediately
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Proof test of lube oil low-low trip | Likely Cause: Set-point within tolerance | Action: Recalibrated PSLL-4504 to 1.5 barg, function tested
- Symptom: Seal gas flow FT-4506 low, buffer pressure unstable | Likely Cause: N2 buffer regulator diaphragm failed | Action: Replaced seal gas regulator, re-established buffer dP
- Symptom: Proof test of KO drum high-high level trip | Likely Cause: Float healthy, minor set-point trim | Action: Verified LSHH-4510 float and trip action

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A rising crosshead vibration trend warns of loose running gear before it trips or fails.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-4501: e.g. PSLL-4504 trips at < 1.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-4501 before working on KC-4501.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
